summary.name: Brackets
summary.one_liner: Brackets is a free, open-source code editor for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with live preview, now succeeded by Phoenix Code.
use_cases: Editing HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files for web pages
Seeing CSS and HTML changes live in the browser
Migrating existing Brackets setups to Phoenix Code
summary.what_it_does: Brackets is a lightweight open-source text editor aimed at web development, with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript support. Its Inline Editors feature lets you view relevant code from another file within the current editor instead of switching tabs. Live Preview connects to a browser so CSS and HTML changes appear on screen in real time. It also offers preprocessor support and an extension ecosystem, with popular extensions including Git, Emmet, Beautify, Markdown Preview, Autoprefixer, and W3C Validation. The page states that Brackets is recommended to be upgraded to Phoenix Code, its successor, which runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, and web browsers.
notable: Inline Editors show code from another file without switching tabs
Live Preview updates the browser in real time as HTML and CSS change
Brackets is succeeded by Phoenix Code, which the page recommends migrating to
Large extension library including Git, Emmet, and Autoprefixer
caveats: The page recommends users move to Phoenix Code, so Brackets is effectively superseded
Platform list for Brackets itself is not stated on this page; Windows, macOS, and Linux are named for Phoenix Code
